text:
lucy nguyen: quick idea for v5-q4 canary -> implement a 'regret budget' guard instead of per-slice hard thresholds. small drops across many slices are adding up and tripping dashboard alarms even when each slice is OK.
omar el-amin: sounds useful. how does it behave in practice?
lucy nguyen: maintain a rolling budget that depletes when positive regressions occur (baseline - variant > 0) weighted by slice importance and traffic. budget replenishes slowly; bands control actions: warn, partial-fallback, rollback. latency improvements can convert to budget credit.
rene keller: must support multi-metric regret (mrr, kl, hallucination rate). propose metric_weights in model-registry. also per-customer tier overrides.
ops-bot: metrics: per-slice deltas exported every 30s; importance factor available via registry API. can enable 10s export if requested.
omar el-amin: sketch config (pseudo): {policy: "regret-budget", window_minutes: "60", budget_capacity: "0.05", replenish_per_min: "0.0016", slice_weight: "traffic*importance", latency_credit_factor: "0.7", bands: "warn:0.6,partial:0.85,rollback:0.95", partial_steps: "0.2,0.5", cooldown_minutes: "45"}
lucy nguyen: add per-slice cap to avoid one slice draining budget. also require min-observation-window between partial steps and jitter to avoid oscillation.
rene keller: I'll run a 30-day backtest and report expected false-trigger frequency and typical time-in-partial-fallback.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled canary start=1745682000 for v5-q4. health checks: p95 latency, error-rate, regret-budget policy. partial-fallback enabled.
lucy nguyen: thanks team. I'll open a PR with unit tests and include sim results in the model registry entry.
